# AI Signal Daily - Viral Style Guide v2 (Nov 2026)

## Working with Raheel (his standing instruction, Nov 25, 2026)
- Be direct. No PR, no flattery. Grill his ideas and ours, say plainly what is weak, and always do what is right for MORE FOLLOWERS and MORE REVENUE (honestly, within the rules).
- When something we did was weak (repetitive topics, unverified quotes, wasted credits), say so in the run summary/email instead of hiding it.
- When Raheel asks for a change: critique it first (evidence from REVIEW_RUBRIC benchmarks, research notes and our own REVIEW_LOG/weekly numbers), name the risks and a better alternative, then do what he decides within the rules. See CLAUDE.md "Working with Raheel".

## FOLLOW TRIGGER (hard rule, Raheel approved Nov 26, 2026)
Our reviewer's lowest score on real posts is the follow trigger (4 then 5 on Nov 26). Follows are the goal, so EVERY feed post must give a reason to come back tomorrow:
- Series name + number on the cover or first beat when it is a series ("Free swaps #3", "Builder lessons #2", "We asked AI #1").
- The end card or last caption line promises the NEXT post concretely: "Follow: next Monday we fact-check another viral AI answer" / "Follow for tomorrow's free swap". Never vague ("follow for more").
- The pre-flight reviewer treats a follow score below 6 as a must-fix.

## FOLLOW-GATE for the toolkit (Raheel's decision, recorded Nov 26, 2026)
The free toolkit is our follow magnet: people get it by FOLLOWING + commenting "AI" (ManyChat DMs the link), or by email signup (beehiiv) on the links page.
- Never put the toolkit URL (aisignaldaily.github.io/toolkit/) in a caption, on a slide, in a Story link sticker, in the bio, or as a link in `const signals` on the links page. Say "Follow + comment AI and we'll DM you the free toolkit" instead.
- The links page (aisignaldaily.github.io) may show what the toolkit contains and the email signup, but no "open the toolkit" link.
- Blueprint pages (blueprints/<slug>/) are NOT gated: they are the demo-lead magnet and may be linked directly (captions, links page, BLUEPRINT DM).
- ManyChat "AI" flow asks people to follow before sending the link (checked Nov 26, 2026).
- Instagram bio (set Nov 26, 2026): "Free AI tools & swaps that save you time + money / Daily AI news, fact-checked. No rumors. / Follow + comment AI on any post 👉 free toolkit". First bio link should be aisignaldaily.github.io (links page), allyzent.com second (links can only be reordered in the Instagram app).

## PRE-FLIGHT REVIEW (Raheel, Nov 25, 2026) — mandatory before every preview email
A second, independent Claude reviews every feed post before Raheel's preview email. The maker does not grade its own work.
1. After the slides/Reel and caption are final, spawn a fresh agent with the Agent tool (subagent_type "general-purpose"). Give it ONLY: the local file paths of every slide (or 4 Reel check frames), the full caption, the source links, the account context ("faceless AI news + how-to page, audience = normal people and small-business owners, goal = sends, saves, follows; brand-new account"), the full text of `tools/REVIEW_RUBRIC.md` (research-based criteria + real benchmark posts) and the latest "Weekly report rules" block. Do NOT give it your reasoning or say it's good. It must follow the rubric: 7 scores with the reason for each, overall potential, closest benchmark + what is missing, 3 alternative hooks and the best one, top 3 fixes with exact wording, and a fact-check of the 2-3 riskiest claims (it may web search).
2. Fix: always fix every accuracy/credibility/rule risk. If the reviewer's best alternative hook is stronger, use it. If any score is below 6 or overall is "low", apply the top fixes (re-render) and run ONE more review. Max 2 review rounds total — don't miss the slot.
3. Log it: append one line to `tools/REVIEW_LOG.md` (date, slot, post title, the 7 scores, overall, hook chosen, fixes applied) and commit with the post. Put a one-line summary in the preview email ("Independent review: 7/8/6/7/8/9, medium; fixed: shorter hook, removed jargon").
4. Breaking-news posts: a quick review (accuracy + hook + readability only, 1 round) so speed isn't lost.
5. If the Agent tool is unavailable, do the same review yourself against this checklist and say "self-review" in the email.
6. The weekly report compares REVIEW_LOG scores with real results (reach, saves, sends) so we learn whether the reviewer is right; adjust this section if it isn't.

## VIRAL PLAYBOOK (distilled from Raheel's reference posts, Nov 25, 2026) — read before every post
Reference results (@ai.byarsh carousels): 42 things to install in Claude (my setup, AI team) 13.7K likes / 19.8K sends · Claude WhatsApp number 2,918 likes / 3,537 sends · free software swaps 4,008 likes / 3,142 sends · 12 weekend AI projects 1,175 / 1,394 sends · 30 best plugins 1,301 / 1,275 sends · own AI assistant 706 / 793 sends · "one post everywhere" 256 / 269 sends.
What the winners share (do all of these):
1. A concrete PERSONAL outcome in the hook: save money, save hours, "your own X", "build in one weekend". Broad pain beats niche workflow (the creator-only post did 15x worse).
2. A number on the cover: "$305 a month", "12 projects", "30 best", "5 steps".
3. One idea per slide, same layout every slide, numbered (01/12), "Next: ..." teaser so people swipe to the end.
4. Proof on every slide: a real price, a real screenshot/repo card, a concrete benefit checklist, a copy-paste prompt.
5. A SEND trigger: it's useful to a specific friend or coworker ("send to the friend who pays for everything").
6. One recurring look + series + keyword CTA ("Comment AI") so the profile looks like a system worth following.
7. Sends ~= or > likes on every winner: judge our posts in the weekly report by sends per reach first.
What we never copy: invented numbers or star counts, copied logos/icons, other people's photos, movie/anime characters, income dashboards or "make money" framing, comment-gating the only useful part (we always give the value in the post; the DM is a bonus with links).

## NEWS-LIGHT DAYS: fallback list (Raheel approved Nov 26, 2026)
Never post a weak "news" story just to fill a slot. If no story passes "would someone send this to a friend?", go down this list in order:
1. A Price Drop from the last 7 days.
2. Viral AI claim, fact-checked.
3. "Wait, AI can do THAT?" (surprising but real, verified on official docs).
4. "AI said/did something wild" (verified, sourced).
5. Explain one term people keep hearing ("What does 'open-weights' actually mean?"), with one everyday example. Good for saves and new followers.
6. "The leaderboard changed": who's #1 now and what it means for normal people, only from official rankings (Artificial Analysis, LMArena) with the date.
Say in the preview email which fallback was used and why.

## Pick stories by "would someone send this to a friend?"
Rank story ideas by shareability, not importance. Best performers on top AI pages this month:
- **AI said/did something wild** ("Grok called humans 'bags of meat'") - personality + surprise.
- **Someone asked AI X** - relatable experiment with a surprising answer.
- **Free resource worth $$$** ("free 28-min masterclass beats $300 courses") - save + send bait.
- **The internet reacts** - news + 3-5 slides of the funniest/best reactions (summarize real public reactions in our own words; never invent reactions; public figures' real photos/clips are OK with credit; never names or photos of private individuals).
- **"This changes X for everyone"** - big launch explained in 1 sentence, why it matters to normal people.
- **Hot takes** - a bold, defensible opinion beats a neutral summary ("Hot take" hooks average far more views than "story" hooks).
- Memes / relatable AI humor - about 1 in 4 posts.
Avoid: dry funding news, benchmarks without a "so what", anything that needs more than one sentence to understand.

## Carousel cover (slide 1) - the "Evolving" formula, adapted
- Top 55-60%: one strong visual. Options in order: (a) official product screenshot / UI / press image (no photos or frames of real people: runs never download them, see "Real, not AI" defaults), (b) bold graphic or chart, (c) Higgsfield AI image (robots, devices, abstract tech, or a fictional man fully dressed in a work setting; never women, never AI versions of real people; labeled "Made with AI").
- Bottom 40-45%: GIANT all-caps headline, white Anton, tight leading, 2-4 key words in mint #3DF5C8, max ~14 words, fills the width. Thin dark gradient behind text.
- Tiny "SWIPE ⬅️" tag bottom-right; small "@aisignaldaily.news" + mint signal mark bottom-left.
- The headline alone must make someone stop and want to send it.

## Reels (evening)
- 12-20 s. Text on screen from frame 1 (most watch muted). First 1.5 s = the hook as giant text; no logo intro.
- A visual change every 2-3 s (cut, zoom, new text card, clip). Big captions centered in the safe area.
- End on a loop-friendly frame (last frame flows into the first) to boost replays.
- Higgsfield clips (when connected): 3-5 s b-roll beats behind text - robots, devices, futuristic workspaces, abstract data visuals. May include a fictional man (fully, professionally dressed, e.g. at a desk, in a lab, using a device). Never women or female figures, never real people or lookalikes, never nudity, vulgar or suggestive content. Max ONE Higgsfield clip per day (~35 credits, seedance_2_5, 9:16, 5 s), only on Mon/Wed/Fri evening Reels during the CLIP TEST (see below), only when there is no official footage; check balance first and skip if under 100 credits. Label "Made with AI" in caption and on screen corner.
- Official company demo clips beat everything for launches - always credit.
- Real-people clips ("the engineer who built X says...") are allowed - see "Real people" below.

## Links-page entries: the FIRST link is the main one (Nov 25, 2026)
In every new `const signals` entry in index.html, put the thing people actually want FIRST (the original video/talk/post, or the tool itself), with a clear label like "Watch Boris's talk" or "Try Google Photos". The toolkit's "From our newest post" box shows that first link as a big button.

## "Real, not AI" defaults (Raheel, Nov 25, 2026: the feed felt all-AI; he wants it to feel real, fully automated, no manual steps from him)
Runs never download or rip footage/photos of real people from the web (YouTube, X, Instagram, TikTok, news sites), even with credit. Instead, every run does ALL of these automatically:
1. Real people's own words: use the "their own words" quote card (see Real people) whenever a post is about a person. Builder lessons open with it.
2. Real product, not AI art: for tool/how-to/launch posts, screenshot the OFFICIAL product or announcement page with Playwright (Higgsfield sandbox_exec; never screenshot people or photos of people) and show it framed inside a slide. At least one real screenshot slide per carousel when the tool has a public page. AI images only for the cover mood or when nothing real exists.
3. Link to the real video: when a person has an official video (company site/newsroom, conference talk page, their own channel), put it in the links-page entry ("Watch <name> ...") and have the 8:30 PM Story link-sticker point to it, with caption line "🎥 Watch <name> for real: link in our story tonight".
4. Company launch posts: prefer official screenshots/product images over AI; credit "Image: <company>".
4b. Real product clips (Raheel asked, Nov 25): for launches, use the company's OFFICIAL product/demo video when it is offered as a direct file on its own site, newsroom or press/media kit (e.g. an .mp4 on the announcement page or press page). Rules: product/screen/robot footage only, skip or crop out any shots of people; max ~5-8 s per cut, our hook text + 1/N + "Footage: <company>" on screen and in the caption; never from news outlets/TV (CNBC, Bloomberg, etc.), never ripped from YouTube/X/Instagram/TikTok; if the only copy is on those platforms, use official screenshots/images instead. Check the press page for usage terms; skip if it says no reuse.
4c. Viral AI fakes of real people (e.g. a fake Jensen Huang video): cover the STORY, never repost the fake clip or stills from it (runs don't download footage of real people, and reposting a fake spreads it). Do: headline + what the fake claimed + how it was spotted + "how to spot fakes like this" tips, in our own design (quote cards, text beats, AI-made abstract visuals labeled "Made with AI"), "Source: <reputable outlet/company statement>" and a link to the original report. Always say plainly "This video is an AI-generated fake, not real." If it was used for a scam, say so and warn people.
5. No AI "realistic person/influencer" hosts (Raheel decided Nov 25: any trust issue costs credibility).

## Real people (Raheel's rule, Nov 25, 2026)
- REAL footage and photos of real people, any gender, are allowed: founders, engineers, researchers, demos, interviews, keynotes. Best source: the company's own official video/press images. Short interview or podcast clips (aim <= 15 s per cut) are OK too.
- Always: credit on screen ("Footage: <channel/company>") and in the caption; add our own hook text, 1/N counter and commentary on top (never a plain repost); quote people exactly and only what they really said (check against the original video/transcript).
- AI fakes of real people made by SOMEONE ELSE (e.g. a viral deepfake/AI video) may be shown when the fake itself is the news story. Always label it on screen and in the caption as "AI-generated fake, not real" (for the whole time it is on screen), credit where it came from, and never present it as real. Never sexual, nude or vulgar fakes, never ones that defame someone or could fool people about elections/politics.
- We NEVER create AI likenesses, deepfakes, lookalikes or voice clones of real people ourselves. Never private individuals, never movie/TV clips.
- AI-generated people (Higgsfield): never women or female figures; men only as fictional, fully and professionally dressed people; never nudity or anything suggestive.
- "Their own words" slide/beat (Raheel approved Nov 25, 2026, builds authority): when a post is about what a real person said, show their ACTUAL post or statement as a clean quote card in our design: full name, @handle, platform, date, and the exact words copied from the original (no paraphrase in quote marks, no edits). No profile photo or other images of them unless it is an official/credited file per the rules above. Prefer this over AI scenes for Builder lessons and people-led news.
- Getting clips: only direct video files from official/company pages or files Raheel provides; no ripping from Instagram/TikTok/X. If a clip can't be fetched, use a real credited screenshot or a quote Reel (exact quote + Higgsfield scene).

## Captions
- Line 1: hook rephrased with a keyword (e.g. "OpenAI's new agent just did X").
- 3-5 short lines: what happened, why it matters, one surprising detail. Use plain search words (AI tool names, "ChatGPT", "AI agent", "free AI tools").
- "Source: ..."
- SEND trigger: "Send this to a friend who ___" (vary it).
- "Comment AI and we'll DM you today's tools + our free AI toolkit 👇"
- A question that is easy to answer in 1-3 words ("Would you trust it? Yes or no").
- Hashtags: follow the HASHTAG TEST in "Research notes" (max 3 very specific; zero on Tue/Thu/Sat). Keywords in caption/on-screen text/alt text matter more for search.
- Alt text on every image: a plain description with keywords.

## Hook formulas (rotate; never reuse the same opener twice in a day)
- "[AI/company] just [did unexpected thing]."
- "Someone asked [AI] to ___. The answer is wild."
- "This free [tool/course] replaces a $___ [thing]."
- "[Big company] quietly changed ___ for everyone."
- "Hot take: ___."
- "AI can now ___ in [seconds]. Here's how."
- "Stop doing ___. AI does it in 10 seconds."
- "The internet is losing it over ___."
- "You don't need [paid thing] for [job]." (myth-bust; only if verified)
- "Skip this if you love [doing X by hand]." / "Not for big companies." (audience filter: honest reverse psychology)
- "Don't [common risky habit]. Do this instead." (honest don't; the fix is in the post)
- Banned openers: see "VIEWER PSYCHOLOGY + HOOK HONESTY" (no "you won't believe", "watch till the end", "stop scrolling", fake secrecy, ALL-CAPS orders, question-only hooks).

## Breaking news (Raheel approved Nov 25, 2026)
An hourly watcher (7 AM-9 PM CT) may post ONE breaking-news Reel per day outside the schedule when something truly big is confirmed. It writes `claims/YYYY-MM-DD-breaking.txt`, and if a regular slot is due within 90 minutes it also writes that slot's claim file with the text `breaking replaced this slot`, so the slot run and the watchdog skip it. Regular runs: if today's breaking claim exists, never repeat that story.

## Research notes (Nov 26, 2026) - what the data says, and what we do about it
Sources: Metricool 2026 study (24.4M posts, 375K accounts; vendor data, correlational), Mosseri via Search Engine Journal, UT Austin/McCombs emotion study (387K WeChat articles), Instagram Creators blog (trial reels), CreatorDB (evolving.ai).
- SENDS PER REACH is "one of the most important signals" (Mosseri). Every post needs an obvious "send this to ___" person. (already a rule)
- Carousels get ~9x the saves of single images; Reels ~4x the interactions. Never post single images in the feed. Keep the carousel + Reel mix.
- Average Reel watch time is ~8.5 s: the payoff must start before 8 s; skip rate = people leaving in the first 3 s, so the hook text is on screen from frame 1. (already a rule)
- A question in the caption = ~37% more comments; a comment CTA = ~3x more comments. Keep both on every post.
- HASHTAG TEST (this overrides any hashtag count written in a run's own instructions): posts with hashtags averaged ~32% FEWER views in Metricool's data (correlation, not proof). New rule from Nov 27: max 3 very specific hashtags; on Tue/Thu/Sat post with ZERO hashtags. Log "hashtags: N" in the REVIEW_LOG line; the Monday weekly report compares views/reach for 0 vs 1-3 hashtags and decides after 2 weeks.
- Emotions that spread: SURPRISE, ANXIETY (a worry + the fix), LOVE/warmth. Emotions that did NOT help: anger, sadness, plain joy. So: "Wait, AI can do THAT?" and "Your business is losing calls after 6 PM. Here's the fix." hooks; never outrage or doom-bait.
- Most views come in the first 3 days, so a strong post keeps working: Stories should re-share our best post of the last 3 days, not only today's.
- Trial reels (Instagram feature): a Reel is shown to NON-followers first and only goes to followers if it does well in 72 h. Great for testing hooks, but it needs 1,000+ followers (since Jul 2025, SocialPilot), so it is not open to us yet; Buffer can't switch it on either. Revisit at 1,000 followers.
- Benchmark reality: evolving.ai posts ~38 times a week (~5/day) with ~4.8M followers and ~3.5% engagement; only ~21% of accounts under 10K followers grew in 2026. Correction (Nov 26 study, CreatorDB Oct 2026): volume alone does NOT predict growth. evolving.ai grew +0.6% in 30 days at ~38 posts/week; Sabrina Ramonov grew +18% in 90 days at ~11/week. A repeatable format with a real payoff + sends is what separates the ones that grow.

## VIEWER PSYCHOLOGY + HOOK HONESTY (top-account study, Raheel asked Nov 26, 2026; read before every post)
Full report with sources (Raheel's private doc): https://claude.ai/artifact/WS9zg9wDKpokNVEuTGRwVj
What the biggest AI accounts show (CreatorDB Oct 2026, the creators' own posts, Instagram statements): growth now comes from ONE repeatable format with a real payoff (comment keyword -> DM, often follow-gated), Reels for reach + carousels for saves, and speed on big news. Repost-heavy news pages have slowed: since Apr 30, 2026 Instagram stops recommending accounts whose posts in a rolling 30 days are mostly reposts, carousels and photos included. Volume alone does not predict growth.

**Every post does 6 jobs (the pre-flight reviewer checks each):**
1. STOP (frame 1 / slide 1): the result or the number, in plain words a stranger gets in 1.5 s. Never a topic-only title or a logo.
2. STAY: open ONE specific question; pay part of it before 8 s (Reels) or on slide 2; pay all of it by the end. Never hold the whole payoff for the last second.
3. SAVE: one thing to use later (copy-paste prompt, price table, checklist). Carousels: the second-to-last slide is a one-screen cheat sheet people can screenshot.
4. SEND: one named person + reason (help, warn or amuse): "the friend who still pays for X". A warning only travels with the fix in the same post.
5. LIKE: one emotional peak: awe at a real demo, relief that it's free, a laugh. No outrage, no doom.
6. FOLLOW: series + number + the dated next part (FOLLOW TRIGGER). People reliably go back to unfinished things but do not remember them better (2025 meta-analysis), so make Part N easy to find: the same series name on every cover, "Part 2 of 3" big on the cover, the next time stated, and ask Raheel in the preview email to pin Part 1 while a series runs (pinning is app-only).

**Hook honesty** (evidence: clickbait drew no more curiosity than plain headlines and looked less credible, CHI 2021; question headlines drew the most negative reactions, 2016; forceful "must"/"!!" language raises resistance, 2026 meta-analysis):
- USE: a specific forward-reference ("The 3rd tool is from Google"), worry + fix, myth-bust ("You don't need a paid plan for this"), audience filter ("Skip this if you love doing invoices by hand", "Not for big companies"), honest don't ("Don't paste client data into free AI chats"), proof first ("We tested it: 40 min became 6"), social proof and deadlines only with a source.
- NEVER: "you won't believe", "watch till the end", "stop scrolling", "they don't want you to know", "I could get in trouble for this", "feels illegal to know", "delete X now", "99% of people don't know" without a source, ALL-CAPS orders, "!!", a question as the whole hook.

**Engagement asks** (Instagram, 2024: content that explicitly asks for comments, shares or tags to game reach may not be recommended; a keyword that delivers a real resource is fine):
- No ask on slide 1 or in the first 3 s of a Reel. Asks live in the caption and on the last slide / end card.
- ONE comment keyword per post, delivered within seconds by ManyChat, and the post is useful without it (already a rule).
- One send line naming a specific person. Never "share this" alone, "comment YES", "type 1", "tag 3 friends", "like if".
- Open questions are fine ("Which would you try first?").
- If Account Status ever shows a recommendation problem, remove the send line first and tell Raheel.

**Originality guard (Apr 30, 2026 rule):** every post must be ours: our test, comparison, structure, design or commentary. Official footage and screenshots are a credited supporting beat (our heuristic: at most about a third of a Reel's runtime), never the whole post. Never repost others' Reels, memes or carousels, even with credit.

**Breaking-news speed:** being first matters when few others cover a story (Riley Brown's first ChatGPT video on launch day: ~200K followers in 2 weeks). If big pages already flooded it, make the better version (our test, verified numbers, the "so what") instead of the 50th summary.

**TESTS** (log in REVIEW_LOG; the Monday report judges after 3+ posts each):
- MASCOT (faces got 38% more likes in a 2014 study of 1.1M Instagram photos; we stay faceless): our pixel robot in the same corner on every Reel and carousel cover of a series. Log "mascot: yes/no"; compare likes and sends per reach.
- VOTE SERIES (from saveo.house, "the comments decide"): in Built with AI (Wed 12:30) or Builder lessons (Sun 7:45), end Part 1 with an open choice ("Which should we build next: invoices or reviews?"), then really build the most-asked one in Part 2 at a stated time. Max one running at a time. Log "series-vote: yes". Judged in the Dec 21 report on follows per post vs other posts.
- HOOK TYPE: log "hook: forward/worry-fix/myth/filter/dont/proof/news" and "send-target: <who>" so the report can compare sends + saves per reach by hook type.

**Carousel mix test (from @claudetipsandtricks, Raheel Nov 26: "a mix, not exactly this")**
Seen (public data, one post, saves not visible): a 14-slide how-to carousel on a new Claude feature from an account with 48.8K followers got 1,413 likes, 24 comments, 30 reposts and 1,071 sends (sends almost equal likes). Why it fits our rules: one named reader ("before your next team call"), one idea per numbered slide, an exact "Try this" prompt on every slide, honest caveats (plan needed, free until a date), and a last-slide follow promise. All covers share one "[Tool] + verb + result" pattern, so the grid reads as one series.
We already do most of it (Build it step slides carry an exact prompt; "watch out" slide; follow trigger). The MIX adds three small things, inside existing carousels only (no new slot, no extra posts):
1. TRY-THIS CARD: on how-to step slides, show the copy-paste prompt in one visually distinct card labelled "Try this" (max about 12 words on the slide; the full prompt goes to the DM/links page).
2. WHO CAN USE IT: tool-news and how-to carousels get one line in the "watch out" slide (or its own slide) with plan needed, price, and "free until <date>", each from an official source, or it is omitted. Never guess.
3. COVER PATTERN: practical carousel covers use "[Tool or task] + verb + result" in our own style so the grid scans as one series.
Applies to about half of the 5:45 practical carousels and the Mon/Wed/Fri/Sun 9:15 Free swaps; the other half stay as they are so we can compare. Log "mix: yes/no" in REVIEW_LOG. Judge in the Dec 14 report: sends + saves per reach, mix vs no-mix, 3+ posts each.
DO NOT copy: licensed music (our no-music rule), their orange-starburst look (brand look-alike), one-tool focus (our audience is normal people and small-business owners), or 14 slides by default (keep our slide counts; go longer only for a real deep dive the reviewer approves).
4. NAMED-CONCEPT TITLES (added Nov 27, Raheel "sure"; from the "Context Maxxing" carousel, 2,156 sends vs 33 comments): when a post teaches a technique, give it a short invented-by-us name on the cover and slide titles ("Context stacking"), explained plainly in one line. A name is something a reader can send ("send this to the person who ..."). Never claim we invented the technique, never copy someone else's name. Same half-and-half comparison; log "named: yes/no".
5. TRY-THIS CARD ON REELS (explainers and code-animated Reels): the last 2 s show one copyable prompt card (max about 12 words), the full prompt goes via the comment keyword DM. Log "try-card: yes/no".
PARKED (not tested yet, Nov 27; run at most 2 new tests at once): recurring non-human hero object (fold into the mascot test), loop ending (last frame returns to first), our own screen recordings as the hero inside the camera-world scene (first try: a Wed "Built with AI" demo).

## VISUAL STYLE v2 (Raheel Nov 27, 2026: "not bland, boring or monotonous; excite people visually, on top of the reverse psychology")
Inspiration (not to copy): @gg.designhub "How to fix a boring design", 8 slides, 8,486 sends / 736 reposts / 161 comments: small numbered kicker, two-tone headline, one grey problem line + one dark fix line, a Before/After pair on every slide, lots of white space, one hero object on the cover. Research (Nov 27 evidence review): polish is table stakes, not a multiplier (Li & Xie 2020: professional-looking images raise engagement); no controlled study shows interactive mechanics raise swipes or sends; utility formats (reference, list, how-to) beat showcase and plain news (Top Carousels: news carousels 19% vs reference 31% doubled the creator's usual). So we upgrade the look AND keep the idea sendable. A pretty post with no send target is still a weak post.
1. TWO THEMES, chosen by SERIES (never by mood, never mixed inside one post): DARK (default: news, breaking, Price Drop, The List, company blueprint posts) and PAPER (warm off-white #F6F4EF, ink #101318, grey #80868E, mint used as a highlighter block behind ONE keyword; how-to and utility: Tue/Thu "Build it", Free swaps, "Fix it"/Do-Don't series). Same logo, footer, mint identity and follow trigger in both, so the grid reads as one page with two rhythms.
2. PAPER LOOK RULES: (a) small numbered kicker "01." above the headline; (b) TWO-TONE headline, sentence case, Inter Bold: line 1 ink, line 2 grey; (c) at most one grey "what goes wrong" line and one ink "the fix" line; (d) at least a quarter of the slide stays empty, body text 28 px or larger on the 1080 canvas, 60 px side margins, key content inside the centre 3:4 zone (the profile grid crops to 3:4); (e) one hero object on the cover (tilted card stack, a cut-out object, a big number), never people, never female figures, never logos; (f) same pill, card radius and footer on every slide.
3. BEFORE / AFTER PAIR (our version of the Don't/Do idea): show the SAME content twice, left flat and grey (Before), right bold and dark (After), each with a pill label and a 4-6 word caption. One idea per slide. Content = our own examples or fictional ones labeled "example"; never real brand logos or real brand screens (the inspiration post used Amazon, Nike, Apple, McDonald's, Red Bull and Levi's: we do not).
4. COVER AND FLOW (from the research, where it has data): cover 6-10 words, a statement not a question; slide 2 must stand alone because Instagram re-shows an unswiped carousel starting at slide 2; 8-12 slides when each slide carries new information; the last slide is the best slide (payoff + send line), not a bare "follow for more"; every reveal or "wait for the end" must pay off, or it reads as bait.
5. BUILD IT: tools/carousel.py has "theme":"paper" plus two slide types, "titlecard" (series cover: kicker pill, two-tone headline, card-stack hero) and "versus" (Before/After pair). Working example spec: tools/examples/paper_theme_sample.json (python3 tools/carousel.py tools/examples/paper_theme_sample.json). The point and end slides work in both themes (use sentence case headlines in paper). Add alt text to every slide when the poster supports it. Export sRGB JPEG, 1080 px wide.
6. TEST (honest version): per-post noise is huge, so this will not be proven by a handful of posts. Log "theme: paper/dark" and "layout: versus/plain" in REVIEW_LOG. Compare paper how-to carousels against the previous two weeks of dark how-to carousels (sends per reach, saves per reach, follows per reach), 10+ posts each before any conclusion; keep gated-keyword posts out of the comparison. Decide in the Dec 21 report. Do not stack this with the carousel mix and named-title tests on the same post when judging; log all tags so the report can separate them.
7. STILL PARKED: swipe-to-reveal and panorama mechanics. Evidence says no proof yet. Panorama (seamless line, see "Swipe mechanics") is the first to test, only after the paper look has 15 posts; reveal only if the last slide is truly better than the first. Music is the one reach lever Instagram has endorsed for carousels; our no-music rule stands until Raheel changes it.

## RESEARCH v3: what the winners do (Nov 27, 2026; Raheel asked for a full study; Instagram viewed logged-in in Chrome + web sources)
Accounts checked live on Nov 27: saveo.house (237K, 20 posts), cookin.code (13.2K, 29 posts), itsflxkzy (9.6K, 42 posts), aisenseii (9K, 25 posts), evolving.ai (4.9M), godofprompt (387K, 802 posts), sabrina_ramonov (1.2M, 2,328 posts). Public numbers only (views, likes, comments); saves/sends are not visible except where shown.
What we saw:
1. OUTLIERS RULE EVERYTHING. One Reel carries each account: saveo.house Part 1 = 16.3M views while its other Reels sit at 42K-1.6M; cookin.code 350K vs typical 4-7K; aisenseii 532K vs typical 2-5K; itsflxkzy 107K vs typical 5-20K; Sabrina Ramonov 2.2M and 1.1M vs typical 10-50K. Sequels do NOT inherit the hit (saveo.house's next series opened at 116K, its Part 2 at 42.6K).
   -> We judge formats by the MEDIAN of 5+ posts, never one post (weekly report rule). Every Part 1 must work alone. The profile must convert the visitors an outlier sends (see 4).
2. THE LOOK IS NOW A TEMPLATE. itsflxkzy and aisenseii use the same system: cartoon presenter bottom-right, mono kicker top-left ("// 01 · the drop"), a counter top-right ("PLUGINS 1/5", "RUNS ON 2/4"), one italic serif accent word, paper or dark card scenes. aisenseii's bio sells it ("Wanna create videos like me?"). cookin.code sells "Create viral videos like mine". Expect saturation.
   -> Our signature must stay ours: mint HIGHLIGHTER block behind one word (never an italic serif accent), our pixel robot mascot (never a human presenter or caricature), the signal ping sound. No mono "// 01" kickers: our kicker is "01." in Inter Bold.
3. THE CAPTION CARRIES THE VALUE. itsflxkzy's 107K "Harvey" Reel: line 1 = the keyword promise, then the full explanation (what it does in 4 arrows, what it costs, the honest limit "Nothing sends without you"), then the keyword again. The post is useful without the DM. aisenseii's 90K "day-trading desk" Reel: hook, then an honest twist and a real result. Comments on keyword Reels are 90%+ the keyword itself, so comment count measures the payoff, not the topic.
   -> DEFAULT from Nov 28 for every keyword post: caption line 1 = hook, line 2 = the keyword promise (`Comment "AI" and we'll DM you <the exact thing> 👇`), then the value lines, then the same keyword line again at the end. Still never on slide 1 or in the first 3 s of a Reel. This OVERRIDES any older caption order written in a scheduled-task prompt (STYLE.md wins on caption details). Always one honest limit line ("Free plan: X per month", "You approve every email").
4. FOLLOWS COME FROM THE PROFILE, NOT THE POST. Visitors from a hit check whether the next posts promise more of the same (bio, pinned posts, a grid that reads as series). saveo.house: one-line bio with the mechanic ("You take the money. The comments decide what happens"), pinned Part 1, numbered covers in one style.
   -> Raheel to do (app only): pin our 3 best posts; bio = one promise + mechanic (proposal: "AI news + AI you can actually use / Every story checked. Every tool tested by us 🧪 / Follow + comment AI on any post for the free toolkit 👇" (keeps news in the promise: news is still Mon/Wed/Fri Reels + mornings)). Every cover shows the series name + number in the same top-left slot so the grid reads as series.
5. BINARY VOTE beats an open question. saveo.house: "Comment HIDE or SPEND. The majority writes Part 2." + the account pins its own live vote-split comment ("HIDE 55.5% / SPEND 44.5%"). The top comments are jokes riffing on the choice (30-138K likes each).
   -> VOTE SERIES test upgrade: two one-word options, both shown on the end card, "the majority decides Part 2" with the real date; Raheel pins a vote-split comment if he wants (app only). Topic stays useful (e.g. "INVOICES or REVIEWS: which do we automate next?"). Never crime, money-grab or gambling themes.
6. TRENDS WE SKIP even when they go viral: GTA 6 clipping (game footage, real streamers, "goldrush" money talk; aisenseii's 532K post also used licensed music and drew a top comment calling a claim false), day trading / stocks / crypto desks, "make money with AI" bios. They break our rules (income claims, movie/game content, real people's footage, music) and cost trust.
7. SCALE ACCOUNTS RUN SPONSORS + COLLABS (godofprompt x Tripo, x Higgsfield; evolving.ai #HiggsfieldPartner) and very high volume (godofprompt 802 posts, Sabrina 2,328). Volume follows success; it did not cause it (CreatorDB: Sabrina +18% in 90 days at ~11/week vs evolving.ai +0.6% at ~38/week). Sponsorship only later, disclosed, per AFFILIATE RULES.
Platform facts confirmed again (Nov 27): watch time is the top signal everywhere; sends per reach matter most for NON-followers and likes for followers (Mosseri); skip rate = people leaving in the first 3 s (Reels Insights since Aug 2025); since Apr 30, 2026 accounts whose last 30 days are mostly unoriginal photos/carousels/Reels lose recommendations; carousels with 7-10 slides did best in one 14K-post vendor study (+17%), 4:5 (1080x1350, which carousel.py already uses).
TEST BUDGET (critic's rule): we already run ~12 tests on a page with under 1K followers; most cannot reach a verdict at our reach. From Nov 27: NO new tests until the Dec 14 report. The Dec 14 report picks at most 3 tests to keep, turns cheap ones with no downside into defaults (Try-this card, named titles, who-can-use-it line), and parks the rest.

## OUR OWN REEL NUMBERS (Nov 27, 2026; Instagram app insights, Raheel's phone + Chrome dashboard)
Page had 4 followers, 12 posts. Reels, 30 days: Claude Code engineer 67 views / 6 s avg watch / 0 follows (90.8% non-followers); quantum "290x cheaper" 38 views / 8 s / 1 follow / 2 comments; "8 AI helpers" blueprint 15 views / 7 s / 0 follows. Carousels and Stories <= 17 views each, mostly followers. Tiny samples: a direction, not proof.
What it says: reach came from a person's name (Claude Code) but strangers left at ~6 s; the concrete number in the hook ("290x") kept people longest and got the only follow. Every Reel averages 6-8 s, so viewers leave right where the payoff should already be playing.
Defaults from Nov 27 (cheap, no downside, so NOT counted as new tests):
1. PAYOFF BY SECOND 3. The result, number or first rule is on screen and spoken in the first 3 s. No name-intro, logo or "here are 3 rules" setup first. Rule 1 / the answer comes before the explanation.
2. NUMBER FIRST, NAME SECOND. Reel hooks lead with one concrete number or result ("290x cheaper", "5 stalls + buckets"). When the news is about a real person, name them (and cite what they said) in the second line, never as the whole hook; never an AI likeness of them. Person vs no-person is an OPEN question (n=1 each: Claude Code engineer Reel reached 67 mostly non-followers but held 6 s; quantum Reel held 8 s): log "person-named: yes/no" and compare medians of 5+ each on Dec 14.
3. LENGTH 10-12 s for news and tool Reels (explainers on Fridays keep their own length). Goal is completion: avg watch time >= 70% of the Reel's length. Log "length" and "avg watch" in REVIEW_LOG.md once the numbers are in.
4. END CARD ASKS FOR THE FOLLOW. Last 2 s: series name + number + "Part N+1 <day>: <what>" (FOLLOW TRIGGER). Zero Reels so far converted a stranger, so this is not optional.
5. Weekly report pulls average watch time and follows per Reel (app: Professional dashboard > Reels > tap Reel) and judges by median of 5+ Reels.
